 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE NIKHIL S. KARIEL
Date : 02/04/2026  ORAL ORDER 1.
Heard learned advocate Mr.Yash Gupta appearing on behalf of the applicant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr.J.K.Shah appearing on behalf of the respondent-State.
2. Rule. Learned APP waives service of rule on behalf of the respondent-State.

3. The applicant has filed this application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for enlarging the applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No.
11215041230001/2023 registered with Cybercrime Police Station, Anand for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 420, 114 of the IPC, Sections 3, 4, 6 of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/26017/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/04/2026 undefined the Prize Chits & Money Vijaybhai Arvindbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71628984/
1 Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, Section 3 of the GPID Act and Section 66(d) of the I.T.Act.
4.
Learned advocate for the applicant would submit that considering the role attributed to the applicant, and nature of the allegation levelled, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail.
It is further submitted that since the charge- sheet is filed no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in jail for indefinite period.
It is further contended that the applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court if released on bail.
5. As against the same, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent - State has vehemently objected to the grant of regular bail.

Learned APP has submitted that looking to the nature of offence and the role attributed to the present applicant as coming out from the charge-sheet, this Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the applicant and the application may be dismissed.
6. I have heard learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers.

Following NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/26017/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/04/2026 undefined aspects are considered:-
i.
The allegation being that the accused had indulged in the offence of luring persons into investing money with them and thereafter not returning the money or the investment.

ii. The fact of the co-accused against whom more serious role had been alleged,
having been considered by this Court inter alia on the ground that he would deposit an amount of Rs.33,00,000/- i.e. half of the money received by him.
iii. The fact that the Hon'ble Apex Court vide order dated 08.09.2025 had modified the said condition.

iv. Considering the same, more particularly, since the role attributed to the co-accused released by this Court vide order dated 28.10.2024, which order was modified by the Hon'ble Apex Court vide order dated 08.09.2025 was more serious than the role attributed to the applicant, this Court is inclined to consider this application.

This Court has taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/26017/2025 ORDER DATED: 02/04/2026 undefined [2012] 1 SCC 40.
7.

In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the applicant in the First Information Report, without discussing the evidence in detail,
prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
8. Hence, the present application is allowed.
